distance_note: Borders Mission Bay North directly along Townsend St and 4th St. OCII's own December 2019 Mission Bay Land Use Map leaves this area (labeled N5A, N6 and N7) without an assigned land use or a drawn boundary, unlike every neighboring Mission Bay North block -- consistent with it still being outside Mission Bay North's own planned build-out.
summary: A 20-acre active Caltrain rail yard and maintenance facility at the nexus of SoMa, Mission Bay and Showplace Square, including the existing 4th & King Street Station itself. Owned by Prologis, with Caltrain holding a perpetual easement to operate rail. SF Planning is processing it as the "SF Railyards Planning Program" (Case No. 2023-000384CWP); Prologis has floated development concepts including roughly 2,500 homes, up to 4 million square feet of commercial space and a tower as tall as 850 feet, via a Development Agreement, the same approval path used for Pier 70, Mission Rock and Potrero Power Station.

milestones.text: Prologis, Caltrain and the City of San Francisco begin public outreach and engagement on the SF Railyards Planning Program.
SF Planning Commission informational presentation on the SF Railyards Planning Program (Case No. 2023-000384CWP); no action taken, informational only.
Prologis submits/firms up a development concept for the site: roughly 2,500 homes and up to 4 million square feet of commercial space, including a tower as tall as 850 feet at 4th and King.

open_questions: Whether Prologis's March 2026 submission constitutes a formal Preliminary Project Assessment/application distinct from the January 2025 informational Case No. 2023-000384CWP, or is still pre-application, is not confirmed here -- SF Planning's project page and hearing calendar are the places to check.

No named individual or group's public position on this specific project (for or against) has been found and sourced yet, distinct from the SF Railyards Working Group's general, collectively-summarized 'conceptual support' described in the January 2025 staff report.

The site's geometry is bounded by real street centerlines on three sides; the fourth (where King St's real centerline data ends short of 7th St, at the I-280 interchange) is a straight closing line, not a surveyed street -- see the geometry file's own accuracy_caveat.
